questions.label: Is the Orrin system full of asteroids?
questions.answer: Yes. Our telescopes see a big asteroid belt there. Big impacts were probably common long ago.

questions.label: What kind of star is it?
questions.answer: A star a little older than our Sun. Our archive photos are 38 years old, of course.

questions.label: Did you hear the signal too?
questions.answer: We picked it up after you left. It repeats every 1.4 seconds… or does it?

questions.label: Any cricket scores?
questions.answer: Your question took 38 years to reach us, so that match finished decades ago. Nice try, Tobo.

cinder.unknownReveal: Our analysis of your data: the iridium layer and crater mean an asteroid impact. But that's not what ended the Orrin.

signal.prompt: Combine the crew's readings. What's sending the signal?

readings.label: Brightness
readings.value: Weak, steady, from one moving point

options.label: Pulsar (spinning dead star)
options.why: Pulsars tick very regularly, but they don't count in prime numbers.

options.label: Orrin probe
options.why: Regular timing PLUS a prime-number pattern = made by someone. It's an Orrin probe!

options.label: X-rays from gas falling into a black hole
options.why: That glow flickers randomly. No neat pattern.

options.label: Flare star
options.why: Flares burst at random, not on a perfect beat.

questions.label: Is there a world like Veil near home?
questions.answer: Yes, Venus! 96% CO₂ and hotter than Mercury, even though it's farther from the Sun.

questions.label: Do stars get brighter as they age?
questions.answer: Yes. Sun-like stars slowly brighten. When our Sun was young it shone about 30% dimmer than it does today.

questions.label: Could oceans really boil away?
questions.answer: If a planet gets hot enough, water vapour rises high and is split apart by starlight. Then the hydrogen escapes to space.

questions.label: Can you send snacks?
questions.answer: Shipped! ETA: 76 years. Please share with Tobo.

veil.unknownReveal: Your data shows thick CO₂, lost oceans and trapped heat: a runaway greenhouse, triggered by a brightening star.

signal.prompt: A new signal from deep space. What is it?

readings.label: Pulse period
readings.value: 0.033 s, precise as an atomic clock

readings.label: Source
readings.value: Tiny, super-dense object in a gas cloud

options.label: Pulsar (spinning dead star)
options.why: A super-precise, super-fast tick from a tiny dense object: a pulsar, the core left over from an exploded star.

options.label: Orrin probe
options.why: No message pattern this time. It's natural.

options.label: X-rays from gas falling into a black hole
options.why: That glow flickers; it doesn't tick perfectly.

options.label: Flare star
options.why: Flares don't repeat 30 times a second!

questions.label: What happens when a star like this ages?
questions.answer: It swells into a red giant, hundreds of times wider, and scorches its inner planets.

questions.label: Will our Sun do this too?
questions.answer: Yes, but in about 5 billion years. Humans have only been around for 300,000. There's lots of time to learn and explore.

questions.label: Can flares hurt spacecraft?
questions.answer: Big flares and the particle storms that follow them can damage electronics and solar panels. Real missions watch space weather.

questions.label: Tobo wants to know if he's a good robot
questions.answer: Tobo, by the time this arrives you'll have been a good robot for 76 more years.

hollow.unknownReveal: Your readings show a star that grew brighter and swelled. The star itself is the cause.

signal.prompt: The black hole region glows. What's making the light?

readings.label: Source
readings.value: A hot swirling disk around a dark centre

options.label: Pulsar (spinning dead star)
options.why: Pulsars tick regularly. This flickers randomly.

options.label: Orrin probe
options.why: There's no pattern or message here.

options.label: X-rays from gas falling into a black hole
options.why: Right! The black hole itself is dark. The X-rays come from gas heated to millions of degrees as it swirls in.

options.label: Flare star
options.why: No star is visible at the centre, just a dark spot.
